description: A million records in SvGrid Base, in Svelte 5. An orders table of 1,000,000 records and every view reads all of it from the server: a view filter for big EU orders, orders grouped by status, a Kanban board with the true size of each lane, a calendar, a Gantt, a gallery, a list, an inbox, a chart and a dashboard. The server runs the view's filter, sort, groups and totals; edits, new orders and deletes go to it by id.
keywords: svelte server side row model database

faq.question: How does a base hold a million records?
faq.answer: It does not hold them. A table on baseSource(ds, { serverRows: true }) has every view read it a part at a time: a grid a block of rows as they come on screen, a Kanban lane its cards, a calendar the dates on screen, a chart or a dashboard the totals the server adds up. The page holds what is in sight.

faq.question: Who runs the view's filter, sort and groups?
faq.answer: The server. Each request carries the view's filter as filterModel.expression, with the sort and the groups. queryRecords from @svgrid/enterprise/base/compute answers it over records a Node server holds, and fieldFilterToSql turns the filter into a SQL WHERE clause for Postgres, MySQL or SQLite.

faq.question: Do edits work on rows the page never loaded in full?
faq.answer: Yes. An edit, a new record and a delete go to the data source by id, so a change to the 900,000th order is one UPDATE. The page's copy of the first records follows, and nothing else is written.

faq.question: Which license does it need?
faq.answer: SvGrid Base is part of the Suite edition of @svgrid/enterprise. Without a key it runs with a watermark, so it can be evaluated as is.
